items.title: A biophysical framework for conscious state transitions based on intrinsic neuronal properties: the dynamic contextual element memory (DCEM) model
items.summary: Unlike artificial systems that execute externally specified commands, the brain constructs contextual representations to guide behaviors that satisfy innate and learned desires generated by the Affective Valuation System (AVS). However, the neural mechanisms by which contextual representations are formed, selected, maintained, and replaced to generate conscious state transitions remain unknown. items.title: Beyond Separability: Closed-Loop Brain Stimulation and the Distribution of Moral Responsibility
items.summary: Adaptive deep brain stimulation (aDBS) and other genuinely closed-loop brain-computer interfaces deliver stimulation according to a learned control policy that is continuously updated by the patient's own neural activity, activity that is itself being shaped by the stimulation. items.title: Creativity beyond the isolated mind: toward a biopsychosocial and sociotechnical perspective
items.summary: Creativity has traditionally been studied at different levels of analysis, focusing on neural mechanisms, cognitive abilities, individual characteristics, or environmental influences. Although each approach has provided important insights, none alone fully explains why the same factors may support creativity under some conditions but constrain it under others, or why creative potential is expressed differently across individuals, domains, developmental stages, and sociocultural contexts. items.title: The brain fatigue syndrome: a cross-diagnostic phenomenon
items.summary: Fatigue arising from diseases or conditions that affect the brain is well recognized. This form of fatigue, brain fatigue, is not comparable to ordinary tiredness that resolves with rest; rather, it reflects a profound and often long-lasting exhaustion. Many individuals struggle in silence, lacking the energy to advocate for their needs. As a result, they may become socially isolated and unable to participate fully in everyday life, despite intact motivation and desire to engage. items.title: A NEUROPSYCHOLINGUISTIC APPROACH-BASED TEACHING MODEL
items.summary: This thesis examines the potential of a neuropsycholinguistic approach to developing an effective teaching model for language education. Neuropsycholinguistics integrates knowledge from linguistics, psychology, and neuroscience to explain how language is perceived, processed, stored, and produced by the human brain. Dissociable Intrinsic Connectivity Networks for Salience Processing and Executive Control
items.summary: Variations in neural circuitry, inherited or acquired, may underlie important individual differences in thought, feeling, and action patterns. We identified a "salience network," anchored by dorsal anterior cingulate (dACC) and orbital frontoinsular cortices with robust connectivity to subcortical and limbic structures, and an "executive-control network" that links dorsolateral frontal and parietal neocortices. items.summary: The purpose of this study was to develop a set of three-syllable words suitable for assessing the Speech Recognition Threshold (SRT) in school-aged children (6 to 12 years old), as there is a gap in the Greek population. items.title: “Descending Enkephalinergic neurons in Barrington’s nucleus gate sex-biased control of micturition”
items.summary: Barrington’s nucleus (Bar) is a brainstem hub essential for lower urinary tract (LUT) function, yet the molecular identity and functional specialization of its neuronal subtypes remain poorly defined. Here, we construct a single-nucleus transcriptional atlas of the murine Bar and identify an excitatory Penk-expressing population (Bar-Penk) critical for LUT regulation. items.title: FieldTrip: Open Source Software for Advanced Analysis of MEG, EEG, and Invasive Electrophysiological Data
items.summary: This paper describes FieldTrip, an open source software package that we developed for the analysis of MEG, EEG, and other electrophysiological data. The software is implemented as a MATLAB toolbox and includes a complete set of consistent and user-friendly high-level functions that allow experimental neuroscientists to analyze experimental data. It includes algorithms for simple and advanced analysis, such as time-frequency analysis using multitapers, source reconstruction using dipoles, distributed sources and beamformers, connectivity analysis, and nonparametric statistical permutation tests

items.title: Social Relationships and Mortality Risk: A Meta-analytic Review
items.summary: BACKGROUND: The quality and quantity of individuals' social relationships has been linked not only to mental health but also to both morbidity and mortality. OBJECTIVES: This meta-analytic review was conducted to determine the extent to which social relationships influence risk for mortality, which aspects of social relationships are most highly predictive, and which factors may moderate the risk. Image processing with ImageJ
items.summary: Wayne Rasband of NIH has created ImageJ, an open source Java-written program that is now at version 1.31 and is used for many imaging applications, including those that that span the gamut from skin analysis to neuroscience. ImageJ is in the public domain and runs on any operating system (OS). ImageJ is easy to use and can do many imaging manipulations. A very large and knowledgeable group makes up the user community for ImageJ. Topics covered are imaging abilities; cross platform; image formats support as of June 2004; extensions, including macros and plug-ins; and imaging library. NIH report
